c11_eng_h_cbse_07_014: Each format reshapes the text — a note condenses, a letter wears a persona. Check: what does the format demand?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_015: 'The Battle of Panipat changed' is a fact — claim what it illustrates instead. Check: what does it prove?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_001: The 'silk' here is exchanged stories, not fabric — and this travelogue is factual, not sci-fi. Check: which genre?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_002: A reflective pause isn't a flashback — the timeline stays linear. Check: memory or present moment?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_003: Altitude, cold and light aren't backdrop — they steer the emotional arc. Check: what changed with the air?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_004: 'Shaggy sentinels' tells you about the narrator's eye, not just the dogs. Check: what does the choice reveal?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_005: Tsetan's storm-driving is a crafted test of surrender — not just 'a good driver'. Check: why this person now?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_006: 'The journey to Kailash' is a topic — the theme is an insight you can trace through the whole text. Check: provable everywhere?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_007: Don't just name 'hospitality' — show how it contrasts the harsh land. Check: how does it work?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_008: The yak-butter tea smell arrives exactly when he enters a home — devices carry structure. Check: why here?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_009: Importance doesn't make a symbol — the mountain must carry the theme. Check: what gap made it ironic?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_010: 'Prostrate' implies submission; 'lying down' is neutral — the choice is the craft. Check: what extra meaning?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_011: Don't just name the tense — 'had been driving' stretches duration before the event. Check: why this form?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_012: One detail isn't a trait — he enjoys thukpa later, so weigh the whole arc. Check: single detail or pattern?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_013: Don't stop at 'the wind was a blade' — ask why a blade, here, now. Check: what does it reveal?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_014: 'Perambulated' isn't better — precision beats thesaurus-swapping. Check: is it simpler and truer?
c11_eng_h_cbse_08_015: 'What happens at Darchen?' is a quiz — ask something the text can argue. Check: does it invite views?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_001: The photo isn't the subject — memory's fragility is; the mother is the girl inside it. Check: who's the child?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_002: The poem does have a plot — it moves through three time frames. Check: what happens in each?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_003: The mood isn't one word — innocent joy gives way to abyssal silence. Check: where does it turn?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_004: The girl paddling and the poet grieving are one arc across time. Check: who's the constant?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_005: Betty and Dolly aren't decoration — they're proof the past was real. Check: what do they testify?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_006: The photo doesn't preserve her — it outlives her, and that gap is the theme. Check: kept or outlived?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_007: 'The sea' is an image — 'nature's permanence vs human transience' is a theme. Check: statement or noun?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_008: 'Transient feet' isn't fast feet — the lives are transient; the feet just carry it. Check: what does 'transient' modify?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_009: Death isn't ironic — the photo holding joy while she dies is. Check: what's the contrast?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_010: 'Transient' belongs to the lives, not the feet — poetic grammar bends meaning. Check: is the epithet transferred?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_011: Concrete 'cardboard' against abstract 'silence' is a choice — ask why, not what. Check: noun or nominalisation?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_012: A tsunami isn't in the text — the dead-for-twelve-years line is. Check: grounded or imagined?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_013: The stanzas aren't three scenes — one consciousness moves through them. Check: who's the constant?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_014: A subtitle covers the whole section — 'Curitiba's buses' ignores two-thirds of it. Check: does it cover all?
c11_eng_h_cbse_09_015: 'It made me sad' isn't analysis — tie the feeling to 'terribly transient'. Check: which words back it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_001: The water cycle is the vehicle — the poem is about how song renews itself. Check: subject or metaphor?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_002: The poem has a plot — the rain narrates its own cycle in answer to a question. Check: what sequence?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_003: The water cycle is the setting — 'eternal' and 'impalpable' craft the reverence. Check: where or how it feels?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_004: The rain doesn't just evaporate — it rises 'impalpable' and speaks. Check: whose voice?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_005: The poet asks first — the dialogue is what personifies the rain. Check: who asked the question?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_006: 'The water cycle' is the topic — the theme is what it says about renewal. Check: what idea does it explore?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_007: Secondary themes here are structural — the poem enacts the cycle it describes. Check: form or content?
c11_eng_h_cbse_10_008: 'Impalpable' and 'song' are imagery too — and the whole cycle maps to making poetry. Check: which sense?
